sn12.63:1.2: On the four fuels see [sn12.11](). Here the Buddha drives home the suffering of dependency with a series of unforgettable similes.
sn12.63:2.9: In the Mahābhārata, Bhīṣma says, “The meat of other animals is like the flesh of one's child” (13,115.010c). Some, however, believed a child’s flesh had magic potency (Kathāsaritsāgara 29d).
sn12.63:4.2: Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 3.1.2.13–17 explains that the cow was once naked, so the gods flayed man and clothed the cow with it. Now a man bleeds when cut even by grass, whereas a cow endures rain and cold and heat.
